What do these words mean?

Theoretical probability is the chance given by our model. Observed proportion is the count of one outcome divided by all trials. A trial is one flip here.

For example, 6 heads in 10 flips is 6 ÷ 10 = 60% observed. That does not turn a fair coin's theoretical chance into 60%.

Compare your recent samples

Each button starts a fresh sample. Larger samples often come closer to the theoretical percentage. The next sample is not guaranteed to be closer or exactly balanced.

CASE 02 / DICE INVESTIGATION

One sum. Many ways.

Roll one fair die, then compare the sums of two independent fair dice.

⚄ + ⚁

Choose your investigation

You may skip or revise your prediction. A likely outcome need not be the most common in every sample.

Run a fresh sample

Every face has a 1 in 6 chance. A two-dice trial records both faces and their sum.

Hint: count the ways

There are 36 equally likely ordered pairs. (1,6) and (6,1) are different pairs. Six pairs make 7, but only (1,1) makes 2. The 11 possible sums are not equally likely.

CASE 03 / FAIR-GAME DESIGNER

A fair share of points.

Two fictional research teams collect points. There is no money, prize or wager.

A = B ?

Write the rules

Roll one fair six-sided die each round. Exactly one team scores; the other gets zero.

First try the starting rules. Can you change the rewards to give equal expected points?

The fairness test

Fair here means equal expected points per round. Expected points are an average predicted by the rules, not a promise for one round or a tie in every match.

Predict, then inspect the arithmetic.

Test the displayed rules
No rounds run with these rules yet.
A worked example

If A scores 1 point on two die faces, A's expected points are 2/6 × 1 = 1/3 per round. If B scores 1 point on four faces, B's expected points are 4/6 × 1 = 2/3. B has an expected advantage. Increasing A's reward to 2 makes both 2/3.

FRESH CASE / A DIFFERENT RANDOM DEVICE

The weather-station token game

A new digital token has a 40% chance of a sun and a 60% chance of a cloud, independently each round. On sun, team A gets 3 points. On cloud, team B gets 2 points. The other team gets zero.

YOUR EVIDENCE NOTEBOOK

Chance, with reasons.

Next investigation

Set an adjustable coin to 70% heads. Before each fresh sample, predict what you might see in 10, 100 and 1,000 flips. Could a larger sample be farther from 70% this time? Use actual results and the model in your explanation.

Remember: probability does not owe you a particular next outcome. Equal expected points does not mean identical totals in a short game.
